discovery: Quantum key distribution: from the BB84 protocol to large-scale quantum-secure communication networks

nominees.name: Charles H. Bennett
nominees.affiliation: IBM Thomas J. Watson Research Center, USA

nominees.name: Jian-Wei Pan
nominees.affiliation: University of Science and Technology of China, Hefei, China

motivation: Bennett and Brassard's 1984 protocol (BB84) showed for the first time that a law of physics, the quantum no-cloning principle, can guarantee the secrecy of communication. It opened quantum information science and, with their co-invention of quantum teleportation (1993), set out the basic operations of the quantum internet. Jian-Wei Pan turned these ideas into physical reality at the largest scales. His group made the first experimental demonstrations of multiphoton entanglement and teleportation, introduced decoy-state and measurement-device-independent QKD over long distances, and used the Micius satellite to carry out satellite-to-ground entanglement distribution, QKD and teleportation over more than 1,000 km. The result was an integrated space-ground network spanning 4,600 km. Together, this work took quantum cryptography from a thought experiment to a working technology, founded on the physics of entanglement and measurement. The 2022 prize recognized tests of entanglement; this prize would recognize its use.
